description: Golden vectors for the 6529 TDH Merkle root. Inputs plus the exact output any correct implementation must produce. Language-neutral on purpose: JSON, not test code.

algorithm.parent: sha256(hex_left . hex_right) — concatenation of the two hex STRINGS, not bytes
algorithm.odd_level: the last node is promoted unchanged

cases.name: single-leaf
cases.note: A tree of one is its own root — no hashing of pairs happens at all.

cases.name: two-leaves
cases.note: The minimal pair: one parent hash over two hex strings.

cases.name: three-leaves-odd-promoted
cases.note: Three leaves. The unpaired leaf is PROMOTED to the next level unchanged, not duplicated. Production's comment says 'duplicate'; its code promotes. Getting this wrong changes the root.

cases.name: four-leaves
cases.note: A full, balanced tree — the only shape where no promotion occurs.

cases.name: ties-broken-by-key
cases.note: Every row ties on tdh, given in reverse key order. Only a secondary sort by consolidation_key ASC produces the expected root. The live API returns rows ordered by tdh alone, so consuming its order verbatim fails here.

cases.name: zero-tdh-excluded
cases.note: Rows at tdh == 0 are served by /oracle/tdh/above/0/entries but are NOT in the tree: the route filters >= 0, the tree is built over > 0. This must produce the same root as 'two-leaves'.

cases.name: five-leaves-promotion-twice
cases.note: Five leaves: promotion happens on two consecutive levels (5 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1).
